metadata.case_name: TAM CHI WA JOEMA v. BOTIN LTD AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: indoor sedentary jobs such as clerk or cashier

injuries.description: contusion injury to her sacral spinal cord
source: I find that Madam Tam suffered contusion injury to her sacral spinal cord as a result of the Accident. The contusion resulted in absence of lower limb muscle power, urinary retention and sensory loss of L1 dermatome on left side initially. But subsequently the left L2 to S1 nerve roots were affected. She is still suffering from low back pain affecting the power and sensation of her left limb caused by the Accident.
injuries.icd_description: Incomplete injury of sacral spinal cord

injuries.description: detrusor hyperreflexia with impaired contractility (neurogenic bladder)
source: On urology side, I find that Madam Tam is suffering from detrusor hyperreflexia with impaired contractility due to neurological dysfunction, ie spinal cord injury resulted from the Accident. With sharp decrease in functional bladder capacity since 2009, the prognosis is poor. She will continue to suffer from urge incontinence and will require diapers or incontinence pads both days and nights. I also find that she has urgency of bowel opening rather than true incontinence. I find that the urology impairment to her whole person is 15%.
I believe and accept that her sexual function is affected as a result of the injury sustained in the Accident. I accept the impairment rating is 8%.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of nerve root of sacral spine

manifestations.description: absence / reduction of left lower limb muscle power (e.g. motor power grade 3/5 in left limb)
sensory loss of left L1 initially and subsequently left L2 to S1 dermatomes
urinary retention (initially) and later urge urinary frequency and urge incontinence; markedly reduced bladder functional capacity (as low as 50 ml)
need to use diapers / incontinence pads day and night
urgency of bowel opening (rather than true faecal incontinence) and occasional faecal incontinence reported
sexual dysfunction including inability to achieve orgasm

treatments_received: admitted to A & E and orthopaedic department of Queen Elizabeth Hospital
facet joint injections (6 injections initially; further injections including one mid-December 2011)
oral oxybutynin (Ditropan), dosage increased to 10 mg three times a day
treatments_future: augmentation cystoplasty (possible major operation to expand bladder)
intermittent catheterization (IMC) may be considered if residual urine increases

losses.description: Residual impairment from sacral spinal cord contusion causing left lower limb weakness, sensory loss and muscle wasting and chronic low back pain.
Difficulty in long period of walking; will have difficulty in long period of walking and should take up sedentary work.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Unable to perform household tasks and cooking when discharged from rehabilitation; awarded compensation for assistance from discharge to 31 May 2007.

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: Sexual function is affected; inability to have sex climax/orgasm.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Requires diapers and dares not go too far from home when going out.
Loss of earning capacity in the labour market due to back pain, need for intermittent facet injections and urinary frequency; lump sum awarded under this head.
